note: Moldavia acknowledged Polish suzerainty periodically from the mid-14th century onward, with Moldavian princes sometimes paying homage to Polish kings. Stephen the Great (1457–1504) maintained the most complex multi-directional diplomacy: fighting the Ottomans (Vaslui, 1475), acknowledging Polish suzerainty (Treaty of Kolomea, 1485), and seeking Western crusade support simultaneously. Poland's protection was unreliable — it failed to prevent Ottoman tributary imposition — but Moldavian princes used the Polish connection as diplomatic leverage and occasionally as a source of military support against internal rivals.

_quarry.structural_significance: Moldavia's Polish connection creates a western diplomatic option that limits Ottoman demands; Stephen the Great's famous victories against the Ottomans are partly enabled by Polish diplomatic backing; the Poland-Moldavia relationship models the 'dual suzerainty' arrangement that allows frontier principalities to maintain autonomy by playing great powers against each other
